body.p: The old Nenets man's son says: "I'll kill polar bears [white bears] in this sea. The old Nenets man says: "It's not a man who killed [this] beast.[OSV:] The verbal form "qÉt-ta-m" (kill-FUT-1SG.S) would be more correct here. How will you cross the sea? The Nenets man lives in a forestless land." His three [OSV:] The brothers crossed the sea in order to kill the polar bear. They set out. This polar bear, he was shooting at the female bear.nominal form "porqÉ¨p" has been edited into "qorqÉ¨p".Then the male polar bear (...), this polar bear was big. Then after having killed it, they cut open its stomach [innards]. And they cut its back into pieces. Then two brothers loaded [the meat] onto the sled. These brothers went home. That middle brother of theirs, the â[OSV:] The verbal form "Éppa" hasone who killed the polar bear, [once] took [part of the meat] home. Then this man got lost, [when the snow] outside was about to start melting. been edited into "ippa". A snowstorm started. He grew quite weak. Then he lay on the sea shore.[OSV:] The verbal form "orÉ¨mpÉ¨lÊ¼É¨mpa" has been edited into "orÉ¨mkÉ¨lÉ¨mpa". He lay there. Then he grew quite weak. Then his fur clothing melted, his shoes. Only [OSV:] The verbal form "ippÉ¨mna" has been edited into "ippÉ¨mpa".[OSV:] "Nop" has been edited into "nÉËt".[then] did he come to. Then he sent [the reindeer] ahead, he cut off the lead in the reindeer harness. Three reindeer oxen started running then. He himself lay there, and slept the rest [of the time]. Then he became very hungry. He [maybe] died, God knows, he slept on the sled. Such a big piece of ice remained under the sled. The whole sea melted.[OSV:] The postpositional form "É¨qÉ¨t" has been edited into "É¨lqÉ¨t". Once somebody said [something], maybe god, maybe a man, running past [with a mouse?], and swaying like that. He tried to get up, he was swaying so badly. Clouds appeared [from behind the horizon?]. The bottom of the [OSV:] The sled and a piece of ice became visible. Then he fell asleep. And somebody sort of asked me (/him) something: A man goes down like that and sways (?). nominal form "ukalÊ¼" has been edited into "ulqalÊ¼".[OSV:] The speaker alternates between the first and the third person singular denoting the protagonist. Then he went out to the top of the shore. He was dying from hunger [looking for food with his eyes]. He got stuck in a hole [OSV:] "aps(É¨t)qo quqo" - "to be famished".in the ground. It happened once. As if the ground is visible (/as if the ground melted) on the sea shore. He was dying from hunger. Then he hardly set out like this: he bent the sled on the ground, he started moving. Then on the back of the [OSV:] "aps(É¨t)qo quqo" - "to be famished".sled he got out to the shore, crawling. Then he got to the top of the shore. Then he lay there. Again somebody said something like this: "A man and a mouse are going down." On the shore, he got to the top by crawling along the small island with purple willow. Then he got to the shore crawling. "I would stand up on my back." He got to the shore crawling. Still no strength.[OSV:] The speaker alternates between third and first person singular denoting the protagonist. Again somebody asked like this: "A man, when walking, doesn't sway like this. [?]" Next to this sea there is a high land. He crawled up. Then he crawled up and looked. At the top he sees: [a winter?] tent made of leather is standing there. Then he fell again. "How will I go [walk] there?" Then, having stood for a while up there, he went down to the tent. A Nenets tent is standing there. The reindeer started walking around the yard. Then he went into the tent. The old [Nenets] man [had] one daughter. Once the old Nenets man said [to his daughter]: "Give this man something to eat." He, this old man, [had] two hundred reindeer. "A beast ate one hundred of my reindeer", said the old man. "You should go outdoors and guard my reindeer." It got dark. He went outdoors. He went outdoors, he's so slow, what will he see [OSV:] The participle form "seqelÊ¼impÉ¨lÊ¼" would there? Then he fell. He lay there. After he came, be more correct here.the beast left. Father and son had earlier guarded the reindeer there and lived outdoors.[OSV:] The nominal form "ÉËtamtij" has been edited into "ÉËtantÉ¨j".Then they gave this man something to eat and he began living there. Then this old man said again: "You should go again and guard the reindeer." The reindeer may not go to the forest. They are sleeping around near the tent." Then he went outdoors, and, having taken a few steps, he fell again. Then he woke up at some point. Who brought [the reindeer] here? It looks like he was alive. Then he came home. The old Nenets man is sleeping in the tent. Then their reindeer always slept in the yard.[OSV:] The nominal form "mÉËt-qÉ¨n" (tent-LOC) would be here more correct. He wore the clothes and the shoes in which he came. Then the third night this happened. "It's like I got well." The old Nenets man's reindeer will not go to the forest. They are walking around the tent. He came back and went to bed again. The next morning, you looked, and [there was?] snow. [If] I, he came, the reindeer will not go to the forest. [?] He turned around [?], when the snow came down, and set out. He went down fine. He became well then.
